source.title: Steering LLMs for Culturally Localized Generation
source.authors: Simran Khanuja; Hongbin Liu; Shu-Jian Zhang; John Lambert; Ming-Qing Chen; Rajiv Mathews; Lun Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE feature extraction and intervention to culturally relevant representations in pretrained LLMs, providing results on whether such features can be identified in this new setting. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper measures culture-related information in residual-stream probes and SAE features, including feature examples and a dataset ablation. Its cultural-generation comparisons use steering deliberately to induce a target culture, so those outcomes are not counted as evidence that the behavior occurs without intervention. Cited results from other work and values used only to select steering strength are also excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Gemma Scope and Llama Scope SAEs as a tool. It selects features by mutual information with country labels, builds Cultural Embeddings, and evaluates steering for cultural localization. It assumes SAE features are 'largely monosemantic' (citing Bricken et al. and Cunningham et al.) and does not test whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recovered by the dictionary. It reports no reconstruction, interpretability-accuracy or neuron-versus-feature comparison. The feature 'interpretations' are Neuronpedia automated explanations looked up for selected features, and the probe measures linear decodability of country labels, not superposition. Its own results bear on its method (bias analysis, steering win rates), not on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly accurate. The authors conclude that cultural knowledge in LLMs is 'partially latent but structurally organized'. They find that SAE-derived Cultural Embeddings reveal regional and country-specific features with a layer hierarchy, show an Anglophone default under underspecified prompts, and that CuE steering improves rarity and often faithfulness, complementing explicit prompting, with gains varying by culture.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts culturally informative SAE features using mutual information, aggregates them into country embeddings, and steers residual activations. It does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method or test its feature-overlap geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature selection changes with dataset construction. Steering strength is selected separately by country, and the paper notes sensitivity to steering strength and SAE-layer choice; steering is applied at all layers for some configurations and every fourth layer for larger configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: MI-selected SAE features on Gemma-2-9B (16K) carry Neuronpedia auto-explanations coherent with country clusters, e.g. an olive-oil feature shared by Mediterranean countries. Early layers hold lexical country-name features and later layers semantic content.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features selected for a downstream label carry domain-coherent automated explanations in an applied setting. This is descriptive and unvalidated, not evidence for superposition.

record.problems: The detailed feature interpretation is concentrated on Gemma-2-9B with the 16K SAE, and the probe experiment is on Gemma-2-9B. Feature explanations are qualitative, and the paper does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units or test superposition geometry. Cultural evaluation uses two LLM judges; culture is operationalized using country labels, which the authors say can flatten intra-country diversity. The paper notes hyperparameter sensitivity.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying rows omitted. Pairwise cultural-generation outcomes are excluded because they measure deliberately steered outputs rather than feature recoverability without inducement.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition, or geometry.
No capacity or importance analysis of polysemantic neurons.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.

Uses SAEs but does not test whether features are distributed across neurons or whether SAEs recover genuine sparse features. There is no reconstruction, interpretability or neuron-baseline evaluation. Interpretations are Neuronpedia auto-labels taken as given.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity. Only an incidental remark that top-MI selections were stable across datasets.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and V4 'supports' are overturned. The paper relies on SAEs as an interpretability tool and evaluates its own steering method. Nothing in it tests superposition or whether dictionaries recover the model's features. The limitations section notes that SAE features 'still hold risks of polysemanticity', but this is a remark, not a result.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension capacity test, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric arrangements.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of capacity competition, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Tests recovery of culturally informative SAE features, but not whether features generally spread across many neurons, nor feature recovery across non-cultural domains.
Does not test SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status as model units.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional subspaces.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Linear probes predicted country labels from residual-stream activations at different layers.
rows.value: 53.2% macro-F1; above 30% macro-F1 at all layers
rows.note: The probe result shows culturally discriminative information in residual-stream representations across layers; it does not itself identify neuron-level feature geometry.
rows.check: Linear probe macro-F1 for country labels (53.2% vs 4.5% chance) shows decodable cultural information. It says nothing about features stored in superposition, spread across neurons, or recovered by an SAE. It is a validation step for the study's own method.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B (16K SAE)
rows.operation_detail: Interpreted high-mutual-information SAE features associated with multiple countries.
rows.measure: Qualitative feature interpretations and country associations
rows.value: Reported shared features for East Asian, British Isles, and Continental European country clusters; a Mediterranean olive-oil feature; and a tea-related feature active across 18 of 22 countries.
rows.note: Examples include feature 38:10325 for olives and olive-oil production and feature 33:5320 for tea-related concepts.
rows.check: Qualitative list of MI-selected SAE features, labelled with Neuronpedia automated explanations. It has no baseline and no accuracy check, and it is not compared with neurons. It describes outputs of the study's selection method rather than testing SAE feature recovery.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B (16K SAE)
rows.value: Reported country-associated features for Indian cuisine and institutions, Japanese governance, Russian sanctions and geopolitics, and other country-specific concepts.
rows.locator: Section 4, RQ2; Appendix F, Tables 6 and 7
rows.note: The paper presents feature explanations and examples, not a quantitative evaluation of interpretation accuracy.
rows.check: Same as R2: country-unique features with auto-explanations. This is descriptive use of the SAE tool, not a test.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B (16K SAE)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the layer distribution and described content of selected SAE features.
rows.value: Early layers were described as capturing lexical identity markers; later layers as encoding richer cultural semantics, including cuisine, institutions, and geopolitics.
rows.note: This is a qualitative hierarchy of culturally selected features, not a test of one-dimensionality or superposition geometry.
rows.check: Qualitative layer hierarchy of selected features (early layers lexical, later layers semantic). It does not bear on superposition or on dictionary recovery as such.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature selection using CANDLE alone with selection using the augmented dataset.

conditions.value: CANDLE only versus full augmented dataset

rows.measure: Number and proportion of selected features; overlap between selected sets
rows.baseline: Full dataset selected features: not stated
rows.value: CANDLE only selected 4,473 features (37.4% of 11,961 total); 888 features were shared with the full-dataset selection.
rows.note: The paper says the highest-mutual-information features were largely consistent, while lower-ranked features varied by dataset.
rows.check: Dataset ablation of the study's own MI feature-selection procedure. These are selection values and should not be a result row on any version. The full-dataset count is not stated; the 'baseline' field is effectively empty.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared the proportion of selected features from layer 0 under two dataset conditions.
rows.measure: Share of selected features from layer 0
rows.note: The authors attribute the larger early-layer share in CANDLE-only data as likely due to explicit country-name tokens in its assertions.
rows.check: Layer-0 share of selected features under two datasets (14.11% vs 0.17%). This is a property of the study's selection method, a selection value rather than a result on a version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Culturally informative representations and SAE features in the tested pretrained LLMs
reader_labels.reason: Country information is linearly decodable, and the authors report shared and country-associated SAE features with interpretable cultural content (R1–R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Feature selections vary with the dataset, and CANDLE-only selection is disproportionately concentrated in layer 0, which the authors link to country-name artifacts (R5–R6).
